definition: A type of autoencoder trained with a sparsity constraint, used in interpretability research to decompose a model's internal activations into a larger set of more individually interpretable features.
details: Sparse autoencoders have become a key tool in mechanistic interpretability for addressing the superposition problem, aiming to find a set of sparse, more monosemantic features underlying a model's dense internal representations.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Here is the short version: A type of autoencoder trained with a sparsity constraint, used in interpretability research to decompose a model's internal activations into a larger set of more individually interpretable features. The part that makes it sing: Sparse autoencoders have become a key tool in mechanistic interpretability for addressing the superposition problem, aiming to find a set of sparse, more monosemantic features underlying a model's dense internal representations. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Sparse Autoencoder — is what makes everything else possible.
